summary: Apple is set to host its annual product announcement event tomorrow, September 9, at 1 p.m. ET, where it is expected to unveil new products. title: ServiceNow Sharpens Its Salesforce Attack With Sweep Acquisition
summary: ServiceNow has acquired Sweep, an Israel-based software company specializing in agentic AI capabilities for enterprise systems. This acquisition is aimed at bolstering ServiceNow's burgeoning CRM push against Salesforce, by enhancing its ability to build AI agents and accelerate enterprise application deployments. The move underscores ServiceNow's strategy to expand its AI-based NOW platform into the CRM market, where it has seen significant growth in its CRM business.

title: Exclusive | Blackstone’s Head of Real Estate Is Leaving the Firm
summary: Nadeem Meghji, Blackstone's global head of real estate, is reportedly leaving the firm. Meghji had taken sole control of Blackstone's real estate business less than a year ago, following the departure of his former co-head, Kathleen McCarthy, in 2025.

title: The Fed will stay on hold through end of year, says Morgan Stanley's Dan Skelly
summary: Dan Skelly, a portfolio manager at Morgan Stanley, believes that the Federal Reserve will maintain its current policy stance for the remainder of the year. He discussed this outlook on "Fast Money," addressing the impact of rising energy prices on inflation and the overall health of the U.S. economy. Skelly also shared his insights on the future direction of the markets.

title: AbbVie (ABBV) Registers a Bigger Fall Than the Market: Important Facts to Note
summary: AbbVie (ABBV) experienced a 2.99% fall in its stock price, which was greater than the overall market's decline. Analysts are optimistic about AbbVie's upcoming earnings report, projecting significant increases in both EPS and revenue compared to the previous year.

title: Camden Property Trust Announces Participation in Upcoming Real Estate Conferences and Provides Third Quarter 2026 Operating Update
summary: Camden Property Trust (NYSE: CPT) announced its participation in three upcoming real estate conferences in September 2026: the Evercore Real Estate Conference, the Barclays Global Financial Services Conference, and the BofA Securities Global Real Estate Conference. title: Merrill Snags $1.2 Billion Morgan Stanley Private Wealth Team in Virginia
summary: Merrill Lynch has successfully recruited a private wealth team, The Aliaskari Group, from Morgan Stanley in McLean, Virginia. This team manages $1.2 billion in assets and generated $5.8 million in revenue, with leader Mehrak Aliaskari returning to Merrill where he started his career. This move is part of Merrill's broader effort to reinvigorate its broker recruiting, following other significant hires from Morgan Stanley, Truist, and Wells Fargo.

title: Northrop Grumman wins $4.8bn Army countermeasure contract
summary: Northrop Grumman Systems Corp. has secured a $4.84 billion firm-fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract from the U.S. Army for the full-rate production of the Common Infrared Countermeasure system. The contract extends through September 30, 2035, and Northrop Grumman was the sole bidder. Work locations and funding will be determined per individual order, managed by the Army Contracting Command in Alabama.

title: BMO Capital initiates Ulta Beauty stock rating at Market Perform
summary: BMO Capital has initiated coverage on Ulta Beauty (NASDAQ: ULTA) with a Market Perform rating and a price target of $580.00, implying a 3% upside. The firm acknowledges Ulta's strong market position and growth but expresses caution due to normalizing comparable store growth and increasing competitive intensity, leading to limited upside potential without clearer evidence of re-acceleration or margin improvement. title: Blackstone explores sale of ZO Skin Health, sources say
summary: Blackstone is reportedly exploring the sale of medical-grade skincare company ZO Skin Health, which could fetch around $2 billion. The investment firm is working with Citigroup and Raymond James on the early-stage sale. ZO Skin Health, founded by dermatologist Dr. Zein Obagi, specializes in physician-distributed skincare products, a segment currently prioritized by strategic buyers due to perceived efficacy and stable demand.

title: Booking Holdings at Citi’s 2026 Global TMT Conference: AI, loyalty lead
summary: Booking Holdings (BKNG) outlined its strategic priorities at Citi’s 2026 Global TMT Conference, emphasizing artificial intelligence, its Genius loyalty program, and broader travel integration through "Connected Trip." The company also detailed efforts to expand in the underpenetrated U.S. alternative accommodations market and leverage Agoda's local expertise for growth in Asia, while consolidating B2B operations for improved efficiency.

title: BMO Capital initiates Ulta Beauty stock rating at Market Perform By Investing.com
summary: BMO Capital has initiated coverage on Ulta Beauty (NASDAQ:ULTA) with a Market Perform rating and a price target of $580.00, implying a 3% upside. title: Booking Holdings stock falls on weaker travel sentiment
summary: Booking Holdings stock experienced a dip following weaker sentiment in the travel sector, despite reporting solid revenues of $7.35 billion and an EPS of $2.54 in its latest quarter. title: Equinix (NASDAQ:EQIX) Insider Michael Shane Paladin Sells 307 Shares of Stock

title: Broadcom CEO Sees AI Value Flowing to Frontier Models and Custom Chips
summary: Broadcom CEO Hock Tan believes that the most significant economic value in AI will concentrate in frontier models and custom chips, with infrastructure being the primary limiting factor for AI expansion. He emphasized that Broadcom is actively supporting leading AI model developers with custom accelerators and has expanded partnerships with companies like OpenAI and Google. Tan also highlighted the use of AI within Broadcom for improving engineering quality and accelerating development, while expecting record cash balance in fiscal 2026, leading to potential capital returns.

title: Why Cleveland’s wage-tax deal leaves Sherwin-Williams little room on hybrid work
summary: A 2020 agreement between Sherwin-Williams and the city of Cleveland, which guaranteed wage taxes in exchange for subsidies for a new downtown headquarters, is likely behind the company's strict five-day in-office mandate. This deal, struck before the widespread adoption of hybrid work, means Cleveland would lose income tax revenue if Sherwin-Williams employees worked remotely outside the city. The hosts of "Today in Ohio" suggest that this incentivizes Sherwin-Williams to enforce in-office work to maintain its tax breaks, despite the challenges it poses for employees and recruitment.

title: BMO Capital initiates Carter’s stock coverage with outperform rating By Investing.com

The firm anticipates the children's apparel company will benefit from new leadership, improved brand relevance, accelerated traffic growth, and a favorable wholesale mix. title: General Mills, Mars, McKee allege sugar price collusion
summary: General Mills, Mars Inc., and McKee Foods Corp. have filed a lawsuit alleging that two major U.S. sugar producers, American Sugar Refining and United Sugar Producers & Refiners, colluded to inflate sugar prices. The companies claim the producers shared "competitively sensitive" data through an independent market analyst, amplifying anticompetitive effects in an industry already benefiting from import restrictions. American Sugar Refining has denied the allegations, stating they are baseless and will be defended in court.

title: Inside Pfizer’s Fight Against Counterfeit Medicine
summary: Pfizer's Vice President of Global Security Operations, Angel Melendez, highlights the significant and growing problem of counterfeit medicine, even in developed countries like the U.S. This illicit trade, which is becoming increasingly sophisticated with the use of AI, poses serious health risks and funds organized crime. Pfizer combats this through its "Detect, Disrupt, Deter, and Impact" campaign, leveraging forensic labs, intelligence sharing, and partnerships with law enforcement and academic institutions to protect patients and maintain public trust.

title: He Had One Company AmEx. Police Say He Opened a Second Card Without Permission and Ran Up $139,487
summary: A former Shreveport company controller, Brett Burdges, is wanted by police for allegedly making $139,487.74 in unauthorized transactions using two American Express business cards. The fraud was discovered when American Express flagged suspicious activity, leading to Burdges' termination and an arrest warrant for access device fraud.
